subject: biology
title: Plant Biology (HL) Adventure 3: Photosynthesis: light reactions and Calvin cycle
welcome_lead: Today you'll split water, pump protons and fix CO₂ via Rubisco.
meta_desc: Biology HL — photosynthesis, light reactions, photolysis, ATP, NADPH, Calvin cycle.
final_note: You learned light reactions split H₂O, pump H⁺ via the ETC, generate ATP + NADPH, and the Calvin cycle fixes CO₂ via Rubisco, making G3P then glucose.

concepts.def: Fixes CO₂ to RuBP in Calvin cycle
Triose phosphate; product of Calvin cycle

walkthroughs.body_html:
In the thylakoid membrane:

- PSII absorbs light, excites e⁻ → ETC → reduces PSI.
- Photolysis of H₂O at PSII replaces e⁻ and releases O₂.
- ETC pumps H⁺ into thylakoid lumen.
- ATP synthase uses H⁺ gradient → ATP (chemiosmosis).
- PSI re-excites e⁻ → reduces NADP⁺ → NADPH.

In the stroma:

1. Carbon fixation: Rubisco joins CO₂ to 5C RuBP → 2× 3-PGA.
2. Reduction: 3-PGA + ATP + NADPH → G3P.
3. Regeneration: 5/6 G3P + ATP → RuBP.
1/6 G3P exits → glucose, sucrose, starch.

6 turns fix 6 CO₂ → net 1 glucose.

Rubisco is the most abundant protein on Earth — but slow (~3 reactions/s) and confuses O₂ with CO₂ (photorespiration).

C4 plants (maize, sugarcane) concentrate CO₂ around Rubisco — efficient at high T. CAM plants (cacti) open stomata at night — efficient in deserts.

Limiting factors: light intensity, CO₂, T. Climate change: rising CO₂ may briefly boost yields, but heat stress and water scarcity offset gains globally.

mcqs.q: Rubisco fixes CO₂ onto which 5C molecule?

numericals.q: How many turns of the Calvin cycle are needed to produce one molecule of glucose (6C)?
numericals.hint: One CO₂ per turn, glucose has 6C
